pr_title: fix zindex to account for group boundaries
pr_body:
Finally fixes https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/1656 ~~completely~~ (alt-drag duplication not fixed yet)

Removed z-index unit tests because the implem is now tightly coupled to appState. Instead, I expanded the integration tests.

- [x] fix z-index sorting inside groups, and across groups
- fix duplicating elements not having their z-index set correctly in relation to groups
	- [x] ctrl-d
	- [ ] alt-drag --- left for another PR

# How it works

(the diagrams below represent the `elements` array, not actual visual canvas representation)

- It does not allow you to sort items outside their group. This applies both to move-by-one and move-to-end.

	![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5153846/91645463-97e17680-ea45-11ea-842d-b9e087fa1828.png)

- It does not allow you to sort items into a group. Instead, it treats a group as an atomic element and skips over it.

	![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5153846/91645454-8304e300-ea45-11ea-8a3b-5b2618aa6a2c.png)

- For legacy reasons, when group elements are scattered among different elements/groups, sorting will skip the ones not belonging to the editing group. This is to allow to manually end up in correct state on legacy scenes if one chooses to.

	![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5153846/91645474-b2b3eb00-ea45-11ea-995a-46369da92ff1.png)

issue_context.title: [grouping] groups should have atomic z-index
comments: Looks like Keynote groups don't have this issue. Ungrouping them doesn't restore the original zindex either.
Yes, Figma and Affinity doesn't retain original z-index either, so I reckon before we group elements we should simply sort them together in the elements array. Easy fix.

Actually, it's not *that* easy a fix. We'll also need to account for z-index ordering within a group (when user edits the group and starts ordering). Maybe other considerations, so will probably leave for after the PR lands.
If we never get to fix it, I wouldn't be sad btw.

> If we never get to fix it, I wouldn't be sad btw.

Why. I can't think of a use case where current behavior makes sense, plus it's best to align with virtually everyone out there.
it's an easy fix, i have a diff for it already
